title: Summer
hook: holidays and rest, and Mass wherever you are
tomorrow: who do you thank for a plate of food?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pentecost: come again, one Spirit with many gifts. After it, the long green weeks come back, and so does vacation.

Out-of-office on, sunscreen in the bag, a rental with a shower nobody can figure out. Summer is when the routine breaks, and Sunday Mass is easy to lose in the shuffle. Jesus once told his worn-out disciples, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Rest is his idea. The question is whether God gets left at home with the houseplants.
screen: `OUT-OF-OFFICE ON.` → `COME APART, AND REST A LITTLE.` → `IS GOD LEFT AT HOME?`

segments.voice: Mark sets the scene: so many people were coming and going that the disciples had no time even to eat. Jesus doesn't scold them for being tired. He takes them away in a boat. Rest is part of the life, not a break from it. And a psalm answers the other half, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "If I take my wings early in the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea: Even there also shall thy hand lead me." No beach is out of range. That's where Mass comes in. The Church asks Catholics to keep Sunday at Mass, and church law says that's met at Mass in any Catholic rite, anywhere. So on vacation you look up the nearest parish, and you might hear the Mass in a language you don't speak. Here's the part to tell a friend tonight: you'll still know where you are. The sign of the cross, the readings, the Holy, holy, the bread lifted up, the Our Father, the sign of peace. In the Roman Rite the shape is the same, and your body knows it. Strangers sing a melody you've never heard, and you stand when they stand. The catechism says the word catholic means universal. One family, many languages, one table.
screen: `NO TIME EVEN TO EAT.` · `EVEN THERE SHALL THY HAND LEAD ME.` · `ANY CATHOLIC RITE, ANYWHERE.` · `CATHOLIC MEANS UNIVERSAL.` · then, large: `GOD ON HOLIDAY TOO.`

segments.voice: Stand up and take a slow walk, even just across the room and back, as if you were somewhere new on vacation. Notice what your feet already know how to do without thinking, the way your body knows the shape of the Mass in any language. As you walk, let the psalm go with you: even there also shall thy hand lead me.
Summer. The season of rest, with God along for the trip and Sunday Mass found wherever you are.
Keep this: God on holiday too, and no beach out of range of that hand. See you tomorrow.

chat.meaning: Church law says Sunday is kept at Mass in any Catholic rite, anywhere. Catholic means universal: the same Mass, many languages.

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an older English Catholic translation of the Bible

rite.meaning: a family of ways the Church celebrates its liturgy

Roman Rite.meaning: the Latin Church's usual way of celebrating the Mass

Our Father.meaning: the prayer Jesus taught, said at every Mass
